newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL's half-year profit hit by higher fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: JAL's half-year profit hit by higher fuel prices.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co. Ltd., Japan's biggest airline, Wednesday said profits tumbled in the first half of the year because of higher fuel prices and the yen's retreat against the dollar.

Japan Airlines reported parent company profit of 5.09 billion yen ($44.7 million) in the first half of its fiscal year ended on Sept. 30, down 60.7 percent from the same period a year ago. Sales rose 6.9 percent to 600.08 billion yen ($5.26 billion).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.

"Although we posted the highest half-year sales ever, the rise in operational costs, mainly higher fuel prices, resulted in the decline in profit," managing director Jiro Sagara told a news conference.

Fuel costs rose by 14.6 billion yen ($128 million) from a year ago, the company said in a statement. The price of international benchmark Brent crude oil has risen by about 28 percent since the beginning of this year.
Profits were also hit by the drop in the yen.

Airlines pay for imported fuel and aircraft replacement parts in dollars, so a weaker yen hurts their earnings by making the prices of these more expensive. A weak yen also makes travelling overseas less attractive for the Japanese, as it makes costs abroad more expensive in yen terms.
Meanwhile Japan Air System Co. Ltd., a smaller airline, was able to offset a rise in costs by launching new domestic flights.
JAS, the country's third largest carrier, said parent current profit rose 44.1 percent to 5.0 billion yen ($43.8 million) as sales grew 8.9 percent to 165.8 billion yen ($1.45 billion).
"The major reason for our profit increase in the six months to September 30 was that we began operating many new routes," a spokesman said, adding JAS inaugurated 14 new domestic routes.
Japan's second largest airline company and largest domestic carrier, All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA), is due to announce its half-year earnings results on Thursday.
